: (per Hon'ble Sri Justice A. Rajasheker Reddy,J) The petitioner seeks to issue a writ of habeas corpus directing the respondents to produce the detenu before this Court and further order him to be released after declaring the order of detention passed by the 2nd respondent vide order of detention dated 19-06-2021 in exercise of power conferred under Sub-section (2) of Section 3 of The Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug Offenders, Goonda,
Immoral Traffic Offenders, Land Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders,
Fertilizer Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (Act 1 of 86), (for brevity, "the PD Act") and the consequential confirmation order passed by the 1st respondent as being illegal, unconstitutional and void and quash the same.

entities.text: Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug Offenders, Goonda
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 03. The 2nd respondent ordered the detention of the detenu on the ground that the detenu has been engaging in unlawful acts of goondaism by committing offences such as attempt to murder, hurt and criminal intimidation in the limits of Khammam Police Commissionerate and creating large scale fear and panic among the general public, affecting the public order adversely apart from disturbing peace and tranquility in the society.
The detenu earlier committed four offences and again committed three more offences which amply demonstrates his habitual nature of committing crimes.
Therefore the detenu has been labelled a "Goonda" as defined in Clause (g) of Section 2 of the Act and the detention order is passed.
The Government accorded approval of the said detention order.

04. The order and the grounds of detention served on the detenu referred to four (4) offences where the detenu is alleged to be involved earlier and three more crimes viz., Cr.Nos.242 of 2021,
Cr.No.258 of 2021 and Cr.No.260 of 2021 of PS Khammam II Town.
05.

Counter affidavit is filed by the 2nd respondent wherein inter- alia it is stated that the impugned order of detention terming the detenu as 'Goonda' has been passed having regard to his habitual indulgence in offences of attempt to murder, hurt and criminal intimidation in an organized manner Mohammad Rafeeda Begum vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 3 January, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83593067/
1 and thereby he has been acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of "public order" apart from disturbing peace, tranquility and social harmony in the Society.

entities.text: Mohammad Rafeeda Begum vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That, there is no basis muchless any merit in the allegation that the detention order was passed in a mechanical manner.
That, as there is every likelihood of the detenu indulging in further such offences, the detention order was passed with a view to prevent him from indulging in such fresh offences.
That the detention order was passed based on the material placed and on arriving at subjective satisfaction.

That, recourse to normal law may not be an effective deterrent to prevent the detenu from indulging in such further activities which would be prejudicial to maintenance of the "public order" in the concerned area.
That, the order of detention passed is an exercise of reasonable anticipation having regard to the criminal cases registered against the detenu.

06. Sri T. Niranjan Reddy, learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the detaining authority while passing the impugned order did not consider the conditions of bail as imposed by the trial Court subjectively except making a cryptic reference that the detenu made persistent efforts to come out from the jail for which he moved several bail petitions, which the detenu under law is entitled to.

Consideration of bail conditions before passing the detention order is held to be mandatory by the Division Bench of this Court in VASANTHU SUMALATHA vs. STATE OF ANDHRA PRADESH (2015 SCC Online Hyd 790).
07.

entities.text: VASANTHU SUMALATHA vs. STATE OF ANDHRA PRADESH (2015 SCC Online Hyd 790)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Government Pleader for Home appearing on behalf of learned Addl.

Advocate General,
on the other hand, submitted that the detenu was enlarged on bail and there is every likelihood of the detenu involving in similar offences and the detenu has already been involved in series of same type of crimes, which are sufficient to cause a feeling of insecurity and fear in the minds of the people at large, the impugned order of detention was passed on subjective satisfaction of the detaining authority.

08. The point that arises for consideration is whether the detention order passed by the 2nd respondent and confirmation order passed by the 1st respondent in the facts and circumstances of the case are sustainable in law?
09.

On careful scrutiny of the grounds of detention, it is to be unreservedly observed that the detaining authority has taken into consideration three crimes mentioned above to arrive at subjective satisfaction which are registered based on the confession of the detenu.
A perusal of the crimes registered are punishable under the penal laws of IPC and those three crimes pertain to affecting specific individual victims and not the general public at large.

All the crimes are registered for the offence punishable under the provisions of IPC and the Telangana Municipal Act, 2019,
conviction in those cases can be secured by adducing appropriate evidence by the prosecution.
In case the detenu involves in any fresh crime, the State can file appropriate application for cancellation of bail on the ground of indulging in such fresh criminal cases if any, while on bail.
The provisions of the PD Act of preventive detention can be invoked against a person if his criminal activities are affecting "public order".
A perusal of the impugned detention order goes to show that the bail order granted to the detenu was only referred.

2 10.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note that even though the detenu was granted bail by the Court concerned, but nowhere in the impugned detention order, the detaining authority considered the conditions imposed in the bail orders, which shows the non application of mind and that the subjective satisfaction arrived at by the detaining authority is without any basis.
11. Here, it is apt to state that acts which are similar in nature, but committed in different contexts and circumstances, might cause different reactions.
In one case, it might affect specific individuals only, and therefore would amount to "law and order" problem, while in another, it might affect the "public order".
Some infractions of law may lead to disturbance of 'law and order', but every infraction of law does not necessarily result in 'public disorder'.
In the instant case, grave as the offences may be, in the given circumstances of the case, they are committed against particular individuals and not the general public at large.

Hence, no inference of disturbance of "public order"
can be drawn.
The subject cases can certainly be tried under the usual criminal law/special law and, if convicted, can certainly be punished by the Court of law.

Thus,
the subject cases do not fall within the ambit of "public order" or "disturbance of public order".
Instead, they fall within the scope of "law and order".
Hence, there was no need for the detaining authority to pass the impugned detention order.
For the foregoing reasons, the impugned orders are legally unsustainable and are liable to be set aside.

12. In view of the above, this Court is of the considered opinion that since the conditions imposed in the bail order granted to the detenu were not considered and that ground alone is sufficient to set aside the detention of the detenu.
Therefore, this Court is not inclined to go into the other grounds raised in the petition.

The issue of non consideration of conditions imposed in bail order was considered by this Court in Vasanthu Sumalatha and others vs. State of Andhra Pradesh [2015 SCC OnLine Hyd 790: (2016) 1 ALT 738(DB)], wherein it was held that non consideration of bail conditions imposed in bail orders vitiates the detention order on the ground of non application of mind.

entities.text: Vasanthu Sumalatha and others vs. State of Andhra Pradesh [2015 SCC OnLine Hyd 790: (2016) 1 ALT 738(DB)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the detaining authority failed to consider the bail conditions, on this sole ground, the impugned detention order is liable to be set aside and is accordingly set aside.

13. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case, the writ petition is allowed and the detention order dated 19.06.2021 passed by the 2nd respondent and the consequential confirmation order passed by the 1st respondent pursuant to the detention order, are hereby set aside.
The respondents are directed to set the detenu (MD Musthafa, S/o.Ghani) at liberty forthwith, if he is not required in any other crime.
The Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending in this Writ Petition shall stand closed.
There shall be no order as to costs.

A.RAJASHEKER REDDY, J ________________ M.LAXMAN, J Dated: 03-01-2022 NRG HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE A.RAJASHEKER REDDY &
